what: Two color plates (echoes) of the same size and corners sit behind the plate. On scroll, each one follows with a delay (every frame it closes .14 and .08 of the remaining gap, max lag × (n/layer count) px), so a color band trails out below the plate and tucks back into place when scrolling stops (trailing). With leading, it runs ahead toward the top instead. With look: velocity, nothing trails. Instead the layers grow up to 1.15 and 1.2 times by scroll speed (|v|/8000) and return in .3 and .4s (power1.out). Each time it opens, the first layer is painted one of accent, orange or navy, and the second one of sky, yellow or light purple.

options.look: trailing (default — drags downward) · leading (leads upward) · velocity (grows with scroll speed)
options.lag: Maximum drag distance (px), default 100 — layer n goes up to lag × n/layer count
options.min: Off below this width (px), default 1000 (original) — velocity defaults to 768
options.colors: When on (default), a random layer color is picked each time it opens. When off, the user’s --fx-echo-1 and --fx-echo-2 are used as given
options.--fx-echo-1 · --fx-echo-2: Layer colors (via style), default var(--kf-accent) · var(--kf-accent-soft)
options.[data-fx-part=layer]: (If missing, two parts are created) Echo layers — placed as the panel’s first children

note: The part sets position: relative·z-index on the panel and lays the panel color once more with ::before — the layer shows only as far as it is pushed out of the panel. The panel must have a background color.

from.where: The .an-echo(data-echo at the end of main.an-content on every page=trailing, a color band is dragged out over the black footer beneath the white body sheet) · index.html .an-echo behind the Hero video (look: velocity — the faster the fixed Hero is scrolled past, the bigger it gets) · original main.js .js-echo / home.js echo layer
